messages:
anna: Heads up — SCIM provisioning started returning 403s ~30m ago for several tenants immediately after the KMS rekey job ran. Not seeing broad SSO failures, seems SCIM-specific.

raj: ugh, that was the scheduled alias swap right? which alias was promoted?

anna: yes. we rotated from alias/scim-v1 -> alias/scim-rot-2026. logs show KMS decrypt errors during provisioning rewrap attempts. sample: 
```
POST /scim/v2/Users 403 
resp: {"error":"provisioning failed","detail":"KMS decrypt failed"}
provisioner=svc-scim tenant=acme corp trace=abc123 extId=" user@example.com "
```

kevin: that extId looks like it has leading/trailing whitespace. could the rewrap job be preserving raw bytes and some callers trim?

anna: exactly — early hypothesis: previous key allowed decrypt of padded bytes but new key+kdf+wrap step exposed literal whitespace in the extId field, so downstream SCIM patching logic mismatches and ends up mapping to a different user -> 403 when provisioning target user not found.

eli: can we short-circuit? revert alias or add fallback alias that points to old key?

kevin: we can create alias/scim-fallback that points to the old key material (if still available) and update the provisioner to try fallback on decrypt error. low-risk and buys time.

anna: audit log shows the old key material still in KMS but scheduled to be deleted in 7d. not yet purged.

oncall: I just spun up a temporary incident: INC-2026. tagging eng-oncall and infra.

security-bot: Incident INC-2026 created by anna — Sev2 — SCIM provisioning 403 after KMS rotation. Playbook: identity-kms-fallback, collect affected tenants, kick rewrap backfill.

raj: plan proposal: 1) create alias/scim-fallback -> old key 2) deploy a short-circuit in provisioner to try fallback alias if primary decrypt fails 3) run a rewrap/backfill to normalize extId values (trim or canonicalize) 4) alert affected customers & monitor audit logs.

anna: agree. also want to capture whether any RBAC role changes happened during rotation that could cause entitlements to be dropped — sanity check the audit trail. looks like no RBAC changes in the window.

kevin: quick commands: 
```bash
# create fallback alias (ops only)
aws kms create-alias --alias-name alias/scim-fallback --target-key-id <old-key-id>
# run rewrap for tenant 1234 (dry-run)
./bin/rewrap --from alias/scim-rot-2026 --to alias/scim-fallback --tenant 1234 --dry-run
```

eli: starting alias creation now. will update when alias ready.

anna: also dumping audit trace for tenant 1234 to S3 for postmortem: s3://redwood-incident/INC-2026/tenant-1234-audit.log

eli: alias/scim-fallback created. provisioning service configured to try fallback on decrypt failure and restarted (deploy 2026.03.23-321).

anna: re-run a small backfill against a test tenant — dry-run shows extId canonicalization fixes mapping for ~98% of users.

kevin: good. schedule a full backfill with rate limiting overnight and continue monitoring metrics and error rate. can someone confirm we will also rotate any tokens that relied on old extId encoding?

raj: will stamp a checklist in INC-2026: token invalidation, notif cadence, audit entries, and PM follow-up.

oncall: added runbook steps and assigned to eli/kevin for mitigation. will update incident channels and send customer notifications if error rate doesn't drop in 2h.

anna: thanks all — leaving this thread pinned to the incident. will write a short postmortem once we stabilize. :white_check_mark:
